subject: AI & Agents
title: Multi-Head Attention: Seeing Multiple Patterns
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Multi-Head Attention: Seeing Multiple Patterns.

hook.text: One attention head tracks grammar. Another tracks meaning. A third tracks sentiment. All run in parallel.

buildup.text: Multi-head attention runs several attention operations simultaneously on the same input.

discovery.text: Each head learns to focus on different relationship types — syntax, coreference, topic.

twist.text: Researchers can visualize what each head focuses on. Some heads specialize in surprising ways.

climax.text: The outputs of all heads are combined, giving the model a rich, multi-perspective view.

punchline.text: Many eyes see more than one.

quiz.question: Why does multi-head attention use multiple heads?
options: Each head captures different types of relationships
More heads make the model faster
Only one head is active at a time

details.summary: Multi-head attention runs several attention operations in parallel, each focusing on different linguistic patterns. One head might track grammar while another follows meaning, allowing rich parallel analysis of text.
details.whyItMatters: Multi-head attention is why Transformers understand language so well. Multiple parallel perspectives capture the many simultaneous relationships in language that a single attention pass would miss.
takeaways: Multiple attention heads analyze text in parallel from different angles
Each head can specialize in different linguistic relationships
This parallel analysis captures richer patterns than single attention

faq.question: What does each attention head do?
faq.answer: Each head learns to focus on different relationship types. Research shows individual heads can specialize in syntax, coreference, or positional patterns. The combined output gives the model a rich, multi-faceted understanding.

faq.question: How many heads do typical models use?
faq.answer: GPT-3 uses 96 attention heads per layer across 96 layers. Smaller models may use 12-32 heads. More heads allow finer-grained parallel analysis but increase computational overhead.
